newsitem.title: USA: Olympic Financial says interest indicated.
newsitem.headline: Olympic Financial says interest indicated.

text.p: Olympic Financial Ltd said on Monday it had received an indication of interest about buying the company.
It said it had hired Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette to assist the board in examining strategic alternatives.
The company also said it had terminated Jeffrey Mack as chairman, president and chief executive officer and as a member of the board "due to philosophical differences with the board."
The company said it had appointed Warren Kantor, a board member, as chairman of the executive committee.
"Olympic Financial Vice Chairman Scott Anderson, who has been overseeing the day-to-day operations of the business, will continue to do so," the company said.
Kantor, a board member since 1995, is an independent businessman, the company said.
Anderson said, "The management team is fully behind the actions of the board, which we believe are in the best interests of the shareholders, customers and employees."
Kantor said he "expects year-end 1996 results to be in line with Wall Street estimates, strongly exceeding last year's reported $1.08 fully diluted earnings per share."

First Call's consensus estimate projects Olympic earnings for the quarter ending October 21 of $0.42 per share, up from $0.30 a year earlier. The consensus for fiscal 1996is $1.64 per share, versus $1.11 in fiscal 1995, according to First Call.
Olympic is a Minneapolis-based consumer finance company and the largest independent provider of automobile financing.
